Data for the 3D Central Valley page (Ali, 2026-11-16: realistic depiction on land cover, before and after with dates;
"Yes, go" to the year-by-year three.js build).

Writes figures/valley_3d/data/:
  dem.png      terrain at 1 km (EPSG:3310): elevation + 500 m = R * 256 + G (m)
  floor.png    300 m grid: R, G = CVHM2 cell index + 1 (little-endian), B = pre-1900 natural type (TYPES), A = 255
  cover.png    300 m grid: R = NLCD 2025 class, G = reservoir: year built - 1800 of the dam a water patch belongs to
               (0 = natural or none), B = 1 on ocean, A = 255
  meta.json    grid, CVHM2 groups and yearly codes (from figures/slider_map/data.json), dams, events, dated canals,
               Tulare 1862 stage, sources

        dem_cop90 (Copernicus GLO-90), nlcd_annual 2025, historic_vegetation/pre1900 (CSU Chico CVHMP).

events.text: Swamp and Overflowed Land Act; wetland loss begins
Reclamation boards to counties; wetlands privatised by about 1870
Canals divert every major Tulare Basin river
Kings River flows routed north into Fresno Slough
More than 20 Tulare Lake reclamation districts (35 by 1940)
Tulare lakebed partly flooded; dry Apr 1919 - Feb 1937
Pumps and wells about double each decade
Sacramento River Flood Control Project (state 1911, federal 1917)
Tulare Lake fully drained (historical max about 1,000 mi²)

Land grading spreads after the Second World War and sharply in the 1960s; laser-guided levelling arrives in the early 1970s; today a high share of rice fields are laser levelled (no California acreage by year found); field-efficiency gain 0-10 %, $400-600 per acre
Red Bluff Diversion and Tehama-Colusa Canal begun (completion about 1980 unconfirmed)
Whiskeytown; Black Butte; Camanche; New Hogan
Kesterson Reservoir: selenium in San Luis Drain water linked to waterbird deformities (1983); State Water Board Order WQ 85-1 (1985); tile-drainage inflows end June 1986

Connelly-Areias-Chandler Rice Straw Burning Reduction Act; phase-down from 1992; paused at 200,000 ac in 1998-2000 (1997 amendment); final step 2001: 25 % of a grower's acreage, at most 125,000 ac basin-wide, disease control only
Winter-flooded rice grows from under 10-15 % of rice area to 40-55 % by the mid-2000s; about 1,217 km2 flooded on average 2004-2025, 0.169 km3 evaporated per season
Gravity irrigation falls from 67 % of farmers (1991) to 43 % (2011); 2001-2010 low-volume (drip, micro-sprinkler) land about +38 %, surface about -37 %

Central Valley Project Improvement Act (Public Law 102-575, signed 30 October 1992): 800,000 AF of CVP yield for fish, wildlife and habitat (section 3406(b)(2)); refuge water supply (sources differ on the volume)

Winter-green share of floor cropland falls; Pettitt change years San Joaquin 1994, Sacramento 1997 (Sacramento 0.303 in the 1980s, 0.112 in the 2020s; San Joaquin 0.254 to 0.160); Tulare change year 2011
CALFED Bay-Delta Program Record of Decision (28 August 2000)

San Joaquin River Restoration: settlement September 2006; Act in Public Law 111-11 (March 2009); interim flows from Friant from 1 October 2009; restoration flows from 1 January 2014 (curtailed 2014-15)
San Joaquin Valley subsidence nearly 1 inch/yr on average, more than 1 ft/yr in places

Delta smelt biological opinion (USFWS, December 2008) and salmon, steelhead and sturgeon opinion (NMFS, June 2009) limit CVP and SWP Delta pumping; DWR projected about -10 % statewide deliveries on average
Delta Reform Act (SBX7 1, November 2009): Delta Stewardship Council (from 3 February 2010), coequal goals; Delta Plan regulations effective 1 September 2013
Drought fallowing: floor idle land 3,594 km2 (2014), 3,872 (2021), 4,148 (2022), against 2,123-2,937 in reference years; rice halved in 2022
Floor crop mix (CDL): almonds 4,508 to 7,156 km2; rice 1,839 to 1,066; alfalfa 3,104 to 1,768; cotton 946 to 576; grass and pasture 12,598 to 10,192; fallow and idle 5,304 to 4,263
Sustainable Groundwater Management Act signed 16 September 2014 (AB 1739, SB 1168, SB 1319)
Tulare Lake reflood: 432 km2 on 2023-05-24; drawdown 2024-02-12; 0.49 km3 (0.43-0.55) evaporated November 2022 to March 2024
SGMA probation: Tulare Lake Subbasin (16 April 2024, the first), Tule Subbasin (17 September 2024); not needed for Kern County (2025), Chowchilla (3 June 2025), Kaweah (2 December 2025)
